provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Original rule: each 4-connected single-colour object on background 8 loses the cells in the two leftmost columns of its bounding box. I tracked where the original 'left' side ends up under each D4 transform. Clockwise rotation sends west to north, east, south and back to west. A row reversal swaps west and east. That gives left for 0 and 6, top for 1 and 7, right for 2 and 4, and bottom for 3 and 5. The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates. It finds the 4-connected same-colour components that are not the background constant palette[8]. For each one it takes the bounding box and sets to the background every cell within 2 of the chosen side. The test is x-x0<2, x1-x<2, y-y0<2 or y1-y<2 depending on the side. Objects 1 or 2 cells thick along that axis vanish entirely. All other cells stay unchanged, and the output has the same shape as the input. The demonstrations are not needed.
draft_notes.limitations: The background is fixed to palette[8], so a background of any other colour is not handled. The generator never produces one. Objects are treated as 4-connected single-colour components, which matches both the generator and the archived solver. If two same-coloured objects touched, they would be merged, but the generator never lets them. The fixtures agree with a uniform rule. These are reasoned guarantees only: I have not run any tests.
